text_read: Repaired digest; then in full from source: §§34-41 and 48-49 of Ch. VI (lines 1105-1300, 1420-1475), Part II §§85-88 (hypnagogic and dream 'Hellsehen', lines 2253-2350), Ch. XII §§146-151 on willed luminous phantasms (lines 3705-3860).
mode_evidence: Müller insists the images are 'wirklich leuchtend', as surely luminous as a pressure phosphene, and sharply distinguishes the moment a merely imagined outline (not luminous, not moving) gives way to figures that suddenly stand luminous 'ohne alle Anregung durch die Vorstellung'. He sees them with closed eyes in waking, by day, in sober reflection.
onset_evidence: Induction: sit, close the eyes, abstract from everything, in a dark place, calm, not just after eating or wine; fasting makes them 'wonderfully' vivid. He holds everyone has traces: whoever lacks them by day can notice them before sleep, and if not then, in dream. Limits: willing a specific image almost never works for him (half-days of practice in the dark; one whole evening trying for red yielded once a red drapery, unbidden); luminous images come only when the 'disposition' is present, sudden and against the will. Willed luminous imaging is extremely rare (Cardano, Goethe, an artist H.) and even then the image transforms on its own.

conditions.posture: Seated or lying; Goethe: head bowed
conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: Closed, fully rested eyes, eye muscles slack; looking into the darkness of the visual field; any eye movement dispels images
conditions.setting: Dark place; any time of day, also before sleep
conditions.duration_and_schedule: Often followed for half an hour; hours of daytime rest; half-days in willed attempts
conditions.prerequisites: Good health, mental calm without passion; not just eaten; no wine; fasting helps
conditions.other: Ward off all thought and judgement; only observe

stages.label: Lichtflecken, Nebel
stages.description: Dark field rich in light-spots, mists, shifting colours.

stages.label: inneres mattes Tageslicht
stages.description: Often the darkness gradually brightens into a dull inner daylight; images follow immediately.

stages.label: leuchtende Bilder
stages.description: Bounded images, faint then clearer, luminous, sometimes coloured, moving and transforming, often at the field's edges; unknown figures, animals, lit rooms.

stages.label: Hellsehen des Traumes
stages.description: Whole field lit as by daylight; one forgets one's bed and the images become dream.

what_to_do_with_light: Observe passively without reflection (reflection and eye movement dispel); hold them as long as possible; do not try to impose content; treat as products of the sense's own life, not objective.
obstacles_and_fixes: Eye movement or reflection dispels: keep eyes and mind still.
Wine and recent eating prevent; fasting intensifies.
Willed imagery stays non-luminous: wait for the disposition; images come unbidden.
cautions: Ecstatic and magical visions falsely ascribe objectivity to these images; superstition worships or fears them.
interpretation: Luminous phantasms are the visual sense's own life (light and colour immanent in the 'Sehsinnsubstanz') excited by plastic imagination; the same images become dreams.
practice_summary: In a dark place, when well, calm and neither fed nor having taken wine, sit or lie and close the eyes. Let them rest completely, with a feeling of slackness in the eye muscles, and sink into the stillness of the eye and the darkness of the field. Refuse all thoughts and judgements; only watch what appears. First come light-spots, mists and drifting colours; often the field slowly brightens to a dull inner daylight, then bounded luminous images appear, faint at first, then clear, moving and changing. Do not move the eyes or start reflecting, or they vanish. Follow them for up to half an hour; before sleep they pass into dream. Fasting strengthens them greatly. Do not expect to summon a chosen image: imagining it keeps it unlit; the luminous figure arrives suddenly, of its own. If nothing comes by day, watch at the edge of sleep.

key_passages.anchor: eigenen Geſchoͤpfen meines Auges. Wenn ich dieſe leuchtenden Bilder beobachten will, ſehe ich bei geſchloſſenen
key_passages.quote: Wenn ich dieſe leuchtenden Bilder beobachten will, ſehe ich bei geſchloſſenen vollkommen ausruhenden Augen in die Dunkelheit des Sehfeldes; mit einem Gefuͤhl der Abſpannung und groͤßten Ruhe in den Augenmuskeln verſenke ich mich ganz in die ſinnliche Ruhe des Auges oder in die Dunkelheit des Sehfeldes. Allen Gedanken, allem Urtheil wehre ich ab
key_passages.paraphrase: Closed, fully rested eyes looking into the dark field; slack eye muscles; sink into the eye's stillness; ward off thought and judgement; only observe.

key_passages.anchor: Ich brauch mich oft nur hinzuſetzen, die Augen zu ſchlieſſen, von Allem
key_passages.paraphrase: By day he need only sit, close the eyes and abstract; in a dark place, calm, not after food or spirits, the images are certain.

key_passages.anchor: Art von innerem mattem Tageslicht. Gleich darauf erſcheinen dann auch die Bilder. Eben ſo merkwuͤrdig als
key_passages.paraphrase: The dark field often brightens gradually into a dull inner daylight before the images appear.

key_passages.anchor: der Sympathie zwiſchen dem Phantaſtiſchen und dem Lichtnerven ein, urploͤtzlich ſtehen Geſtalten leuchtend da,
key_passages.paraphrase: What he imagines stays an unlit outline; suddenly luminous figures stand there unprompted, as surely luminous as a pressure phosphene; 'I do not see what I would like to see'.

key_passages.anchor: und beſonders, wenn ich gefaſtet habe. Durch Faſten kann ich dieſe Phaenomene zu einer wunderbaren Lebendigkeit
key_passages.paraphrase: Easiest when well and unexcited, especially after fasting, which makes them wonderfully vivid; never after wine.

key_passages.anchor: ſo habe ich doch bei der groͤßten Anſtrengung faſt nie willkuͤhrlich ein beſtimmtes Phantasma von
key_passages.paraphrase: Despite half-days of willed practice in the dark he could almost never produce a chosen luminous image or fix a colour; one evening of trying for red yielded once, suddenly, a red drapery he had not imagined.
